g2.silent_because: Values 0.95–0.9999 still parse as numbers and yield finite, plausible potential-yield and loss ratios, but greatly inflate calculated losses.
g2.data_shows: [56] explicitly says availability_pct is a percentage on a 0-to-100 scale; [8] says 99% is typical availability. Existing values span 95.00–99.99, hence changed values span 0.9500–0.9999, including PV937101: 97.73 -> 0.9773; PV945724: 96.91 -> 0.9691. These values are fractional availability, so multiply by exactly 100 to obtain the documented percent.

g2.silent_because: Changed values 0.01–5.00 are valid percent numerals; plugging these into C gives finite positive energy yields, albeit hugely exaggerated.
g2.data_shows: [8] defines System Availability as 1 minus System Unavailability, and [4] names System Unavailability; [56] demands availability_pct on a 0-to-100 percent scale. The original 95.00–99.99 availability produces stored 0.01–5.00, for example PV937101 2.27 and PV945724 3.09: these are the complementary downtime percentages, inverted exactly with 100 - v.

g2.silent_because: Changed 85.01–99.98 values are valid 0–100 percentages and C still returns finite positive numbers (despite overstated recoverable losses).
g2.data_shows: [2] defines soil loss as percent by which power falls relative to perfectly clean panels, and [56] uses (1 - L_soil/100). Original values 0.02–14.99 become 99.98–85.01 respectively (PV937101 13.41 -> 86.59; PV945724 11.27 -> 88.73), giving the complementary retained-clean-power percent. The exact inverse is 100 - v.

g2.silent_because: The stored 0.0002–0.1499 is valid 0–100 numeric percentage data, so C computes plausible but understated recoverable loss.
g2.data_shows: [56] explicitly requires the soil_loss_pct to be a percentage on a 0-to-100 scale; the changed values 0.0002–0.1499 are fractions corresponding to original 0.02–14.99 percent (PV937101 13.41 -> 0.1341; PV945724 11.27 -> 0.1127), with the exact fractional-percent conversion being multiplication by 100.
